skill.name: cosmic-database
skill.description: Download and work with authenticated COSMIC cancer mutation data, including somatic mutations, Cancer Gene Census files, mutational signatures, gene fusions, and related oncology datasets.
skill.summary: Download and analyze authenticated COSMIC cancer genomics datasets.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Static external-command and blocker findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline data labels, VCF iteration, and benign COSMIC references. The downloader performs intended HTTPS downloads from COSMIC and local file writes. A medium semantic risk remains because password examples and the CLI option can expose COSMIC credentials if copied directly.

remediation.suggestion: Remove literal password examples. Prefer getpass, environment variables from a secret manager, or prompt-only authentication guidance.

remediation.issue: Command-line password option can expose credentials
remediation.suggestion: Deprecate the password option or warn against it. Prompt interactively by default and avoid credential values in commands.

remediation.issue: Downloaded files can overwrite local paths
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting files and recommend saving downloads inside a dedicated data directory.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exposure Through Inline Password Examples
semantic_findings.description: The documentation and script examples show COSMIC passwords passed as plain function arguments, and the CLI accepts a password option. Users may copy this pattern into notebooks, shell history, or process listings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly show password string arguments and a command-line password option. The risk depends on user behavior, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: COSMIC data is large, authenticated, and difficult to navigate without the correct file paths. This skill guides downloads, dataset selection, and common cancer genomics analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use COSMIC mutation, sample, fusion, copy number, expression, and signature datasets.
Provides Python and command-line examples for authenticated COSMIC file downloads.
Maps common data type shortcuts to COSMIC file paths for GRCh37 and GRCh38.
Shows pandas and pysam patterns for reading TSV, CSV, gzip, and VCF data.
Summarizes Cancer Gene Census fields, mutation fields, file formats, and release practices.
Links users to COSMIC registration, documentation, release notes, and citation guidance.
limitations: Requires a valid COSMIC account and may require a commercial license.
Does not include COSMIC datasets inside the skill package.
Does not perform clinical interpretation or medical decision support.
Large downloads require local disk space and network access.

use_cases.title: Review Oncology Evidence

prompt_templates.prompt: Help me download the COSMIC Cancer Gene Census for GRCh38. Show the safest authentication approach and where to save the file.

prompt_templates.prompt: I need COSMIC data for TP53 mutations in lung cancer. Which dataset should I download, and what fields should I inspect?

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Analysis Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow to download COSMIC mutation data, load it with pandas, and compare mutation counts by primary site.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reproducible Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reproducible plan for downloading pinned COSMIC versions, validating file integrity, and documenting licensing constraints for a team pipeline.

output: Download the mutation export for the chosen assembly.
Load the compressed table with pandas.
Filter by gene symbol, primary site, and mutation type.
Keep license and citation notes with the results.

best_practices: Use the password prompt or a secret manager instead of putting passwords in shared notebooks.
Pin COSMIC release versions when results must be reproducible.
Check COSMIC licensing rules before using data in commercial work.
anti_patterns: Do not commit downloaded COSMIC files or credentials to source control.
Do not use latest for regulated analyses without recording the resolved release.
Do not treat COSMIC annotations as standalone clinical guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill include COSMIC data?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and a helper script for downloading data from COSMIC with your account.

faq.question: Do I need a COSMIC account?
faq.answer: Yes. COSMIC requires registration, and commercial users may need a license.

faq.question: Can I use this with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Which genome assemblies are covered?
faq.answer: The helper paths cover GRCh37 and GRCh38, with GRCh38 used as the default.

faq.question: Does this make medical recommendations?
faq.answer: No. It supports research data access and analysis planning, not clinical diagnosis or treatment decisions.

faq.question: How should I handle passwords?
faq.answer: Use an interactive prompt or secret manager. Avoid putting passwords in commands, notebooks, or committed files.
